reason: The text explicitly references Yahweh's goals toward the Hebrew people through Joshua's words in the covenant negotiation. Specifically, it states that Yahweh commanded Moses 'to give you all the land' (לָתֵ֤ת לָכֶם֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ) and 'to destroy all the inhabitants of the land before you' (לְהַשְׁמִ֛יד אֶת־ כָּל־ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֑ם). These are presented as Yahweh's stated purposes for the Hebrew people, aimed at securing the land for them and removing obstacles to their settlement. The Gibeonites' claim to have come 'for the name of Yahweh your God' also acknowledges this divine initiative toward Israel.
